claims.claim: The C4 corpus construction described with T5 uses language identification, heuristic filtering, deduplication and removal of noisy or inappropriate content.
claims.notes: The rules are specific to the English C4 construction and should not be treated as universal thresholds.

claims.claim: CCNet adds a language-model perplexity filter to a web-corpus pipeline to select documents closer to high-quality reference corpora such as Wikipedia.
claims.notes: Perplexity measures fit to a chosen reference distribution, not universal truth or quality.

claims.claim: Dolma documents Bloom-filter-based deduplication for document keys or paragraph spans, while DataTrove provides a multi-stage MinHash workflow for approximate document deduplication.
claims.notes: Exact and approximate deduplication have different error profiles; a candidate similarity is not proof of semantic redundancy.

claims.claim: DCLM evaluates data curation methods under a standardized raw pool and downstream training/evaluation setup, making downstream utility a central comparison signal.
claims.notes: A filter ranking is conditional on the model, data pool, compute budget, tokenizer and evaluation suite.

claims.claim: The LLM Data Auditor framework distinguishes synthetic-data quality from trustworthiness and surveys intrinsic metrics as well as evaluation practice.
claims.notes: LLM-judge scores are one measurement source and should be calibrated and audited rather than treated as ground truth.

claims.claim: A 2025 survey of LLM datasets describes a broad preprocessing workflow including collection, filtering, deduplication, standardization and review.
claims.notes: This is a survey-level synthesis, not a mandated order for every production pipeline.

claims.claim: Precision, recall and F1 can be computed from TP, FP and FN as TP/(TP+FP), TP/(TP+FN), and 2PR/(P+R), respectively.
claims.notes: The positive class must be explicitly defined; when removal is positive, false positives represent good data incorrectly discarded.

claims.claim: Filtering decisions should be audited for retained-distribution changes and false-positive costs, not evaluated only by a single aggregate accuracy score.
claims.locator: DCLM standardized curation comparisons and downstream evaluation; engineering synthesis
claims.notes: Report slices, confidence intervals, data retention and the controlled downstream recipe.

claims.claim: License, privacy, safety and benchmark decontamination constraints should be treated as eligibility or governance gates rather than values that can be compensated by a high quality score.
claims.locator: Datasheets for Datasets; data collection, distribution and maintenance questions
claims.notes: This is an engineering governance recommendation; actual legal obligations depend on source, jurisdiction and intended use.
